title: Can we unlearn implicit biases? With Mahzarin Banaji, PhD

sentences.en: Over the past several decades, the term implicit bias has moved from the relative obscurity of academia into everyday usage.
sentences.zh: 在过去几十年里，“内隐偏见”这一术语已从相对冷门的学术领域进入了日常用语中。

sentences.en: The concept is also at the center of recent debates over how society should think about and teach about racism, prejudice, and discrimination.
sentences.zh: 这一概念也是近期关于社会应如何思考和教授种族主义、偏见和歧视等议题的核心。

sentences.en: The idea that we all have biases that operate below the level of our conscious thought may be uncomfortable,
sentences.zh: 我们每个人都存在潜意识层面的偏见，这一观点可能会让人感到不安，

sentences.en: but decades of research have found that many people who would never consciously agree
sentences.zh: 但几十年的研究发现，许多人即便在意识层面绝不会认同

sentences.en: with prejudice statements about black people, LGBTQ people, or women, for example, can nonetheless harbor implicit biases toward these groups and others.
sentences.zh: 针对黑人、LGBTQ群体或女性等群体的偏见言论，却依然可能对这些群体及其他人持有内隐偏见。

sentences.en: So what is implicit bias and where does it come from?
sentences.zh: 那么，什么是内隐偏见？它从何而来？

sentences.en: What's the connection between implicit bias and prejudice?
sentences.zh: 内隐偏见与偏见之间有什么联系？

sentences.en: How are they different and how are they connected?
sentences.zh: 它们有何不同，又如何相互关联？

sentences.en: How do implicit biases influence our behavior?
sentences.zh: 内隐偏见如何影响我们的行为？

sentences.en: Is it possible to unlearn or overcome our biases?
sentences.zh: 我们有可能消除或克服这些偏见吗？

sentences.en: Does educating people about implicit bias help to reduce it?
sentences.zh: 对人们进行内隐偏见教育有助于减少它吗？

sentences.en: And as a society, are we shedding any of our biases?
sentences.zh: 作为一个社会，我们是否正在摆脱某些偏见？

sentences.en: Do they remain as strong as ever?
sentences.zh: 还是说它们依然根深蒂固？

sentences.en: Welcome to Speaking of Psychology, the flagship podcast of the American Psychological Association that examines the connections between psychological science and everyday life.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听美国心理学会的旗舰播客《心理学谈话》，我们将探讨心理科学与日常生活之间的联系。

sentences.en: I'm Kim Mills.
sentences.zh: 我是主持人 Kim Mills。

sentences.en: Our guest today is Dr. Mazarin Banaji.
sentences.zh: 我们今天的嘉宾是 Mazarin Banaji 博士。

sentences.en: Dr. Banaji is a professor of psychology at Harvard University and a pioneer in researching implicit bias.
sentences.zh: Banaji 博士是哈佛大学心理学教授，也是内隐偏见研究的先驱。

sentences.en: Together with her colleague, Anthony Greenwald, she coined the term and ran the first studies on it in the 1990s.
sentences.zh: 她与同事 Anthony Greenwald 在20世纪90年代共同提出了这一术语，并开展了最初的相关研究。

sentences.en: Today, Dr. Banaji continues to study the disparity between what people think they believe and their thoughts and feelings that operate on an unconscious level.
sentences.zh: 如今，Banaji 博士继续研究人们自认为的信念与潜意识层面的思想和感受之间的差异。

sentences.en: She is co-author of the 2013 book, Blind Spot,
sentences.zh: 她是2013年出版的著作《盲点》的合著者，

sentences.en: Hidden Biases of Good People, and has won many awards and honors for her work, including most recently,
sentences.zh: 该书全名为《盲点：好人的隐性偏见》，她因其研究工作赢得了许多奖项和荣誉，最近的一项是，

sentences.en: the 2022 Atkinson Prize in Psychological and Cognitive Sciences from the National Academy of Sciences.
sentences.zh: 美国国家科学院颁发的2022年阿特金森心理与认知科学奖。

sentences.en: She also won APA's 2017 award for Distinguished Scientific Contributions.
sentences.zh: 她还获得了美国心理学会2017年杰出科学贡献奖。

sentences.en: Thank you for joining me today,
sentences.zh: 感谢您今天参加节目，

sentences.en: Dr. Banaji.
sentences.zh: Banaji 博士。

sentences.en: Thank you for having me.
sentences.zh: 谢谢邀请。

sentences.en: In the public discussion over implicit bias, the term often gets conflated with prejudice or racism.
sentences.zh: 在关于内隐偏见的公众讨论中，这个术语经常与偏见或种族主义混为一谈。

sentences.en: Can you start our discussion by explaining what implicit bias is and how it's different from bias and prejudice?
sentences.zh: 您能先解释一下什么是内隐偏见，以及它与普通偏见有何不同吗？

sentences.en: Implicit bias is definitely not racism.
sentences.zh: 内隐偏见绝对不等同于种族主义。

sentences.en: It gets used that way, but that's incorrect.
sentences.zh: 人们常那样使用这个词，但那是不准确的。

sentences.en: For much of the 20th century, social psychologists who were interested in the topic of prejudice and how could they not be, the field almost got its start during the war years,
sentences.zh: 在20世纪的大部分时间里，对偏见课题感兴趣的社会心理学家们——他们怎么可能不感兴趣呢，这个领域几乎是在战争年代起步的，

sentences.en: during World War II, when larger numbers of scholars and scientists from Germany were coming to the
sentences.zh: 也就是二战期间，当时大量来自德国的学者和科学家来到

sentences.en: United States.
sentences.zh: 美国。

sentences.en: For some reason, on the top of their mind was the topic of prejudice.
sentences.zh: 出于某种原因，他们最关心的就是偏见这个话题。

sentences.en: So they studied it in the way in which they could.
sentences.zh: 于是他们尽其所能地对此进行了研究。

sentences.en: They asked people questions about who they loved and hated.
sentences.zh: 他们询问人们关于爱与恨的问题。

sentences.en: They asked people more subtle questions about the kinds of policies they might support to try to get at this concept called prejudice.
sentences.zh: 他们向人们提出更微妙的问题，询问他们可能支持什么样的政策，试图借此触及“偏见”这一概念。

sentences.en: Prejudice to psychologists is an explicit, conscious, aversion, or dislike that one person may have towards groups of people.
sentences.zh: 对心理学家而言，偏见是一种显性的、有意识的厌恶或反感，是一个人对特定群体可能持有的态度。

sentences.en: If I were to say to you, I do not think that women should be teaching at Harvard, that would be an example of something we would call a conscious prejudice.
sentences.zh: 如果我对你说，“我不认为女性应该在哈佛任教”，这就是我们所说的“有意识的偏见”的一个例子。

sentences.en: What we've studied, and what the invention of computers that allowed us to do experiments that would get at other
sentences.zh: 而我们所研究的，以及计算机的发明让我们能够进行实验去触及我们大脑的其他

sentences.en: levels of our minds, what that work revealed was that a large number of people in our society have genuinely, honestly come to a point where they believe that they are not biased.
sentences.zh: 层面，这些工作揭示出：我们社会中的许多人已经真诚、诚实地认为自己没有偏见。

sentences.en: And that, I would argue, is true.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为，这是事实。

sentences.en: This is not something that they're making up.
sentences.zh: 这不是他们编造出来的。

sentences.en: This is not something that they're lying about.
sentences.zh: 这不是他们在撒谎。

sentences.en: They genuinely believe in the ideals of egalitarianism, equal treatment, fair treatment, and they disavow prejudice.
sentences.zh: 他们真诚地相信平等主义、平等对待、公平对待的理想，并且否认偏见。

sentences.en: They teach their children how to not be prejudiced, and so on.
sentences.zh: 他们教导孩子不要有偏见，等等。

sentences.en: And yet, what our evidence showed is that those very same people, I would say people like your listeners, people like myself,
sentences.zh: 然而，我们的证据表明，正是这些人——我想说，就像你们的听众，就像我自己，

sentences.en: we found that we do have what we call implicit levels of bias.
sentences.zh: 我们发现我们确实存在所谓的“内隐偏见”。

sentences.en: It is not at all the same thing as racism or sexism, but it indeed is evidence of an association in our heads that I would call the roots of prejudice.
sentences.zh: 这与种族主义或性别歧视完全不是一回事，但它确实是我们头脑中某种联想的证据，我称之为偏见的根源。

sentences.en: Where do these implicit biases come from?
sentences.zh: 这些内隐偏见从何而来？

sentences.en: How do we learn them since we're not really aware of them?
sentences.zh: 既然我们并没有真正意识到它们，我们是如何习得它们的呢？

sentences.en: You're right to use the word learn because we're not born knowing that
sentences.zh: 你用“习得”这个词很准确，因为我们并非生来就知道

sentences.en: African-Americans are bad and white people or European-Americans are good.
sentences.zh: 非裔美国人是坏的，而白人或欧裔美国人是好的。

sentences.en: We're not born into the world believing that men should be going out to work and women should be at home.
sentences.zh: 我们并非生来就相信男人应该出去工作，女人应该待在家里。

sentences.en: So learning is what happens.
sentences.zh: 所以，这就是习得的过程。

sentences.en: But it would be remiss, I think, not to speak a little bit about what we mean here by learning.
sentences.zh: 但我认为，如果不谈谈我们这里所说的“习得”是指什么，那就太失职了。

sentences.en: What we mean here by learning is something that happens extremely fast, quite early in life, and then progresses.
sentences.zh: 我们所说的习得，是指在生命早期极快发生并持续发展的东西。

sentences.en: And that comes not from just the social environment, but by the structure and the architecture of our minds, the way our brain got built over a period of evolutionary history.
sentences.zh: 这不仅源于社会环境，还源于我们大脑的结构和架构，也就是我们大脑在漫长的进化历史中形成的方式。

sentences.en: So we have a certain kind of a brain as humans, and we tend to focus on the conscious aspects of what our minds allow us to do.
sentences.zh: 作为人类，我们拥有特定类型的大脑，我们倾向于关注大脑允许我们进行的有意识活动。

sentences.en: I consciously logged in today, you are consciously speaking to me today about the topic of implicit bias.
sentences.zh: 我今天是有意识地登录的，你今天也是有意识地在和我谈论内隐偏见这个话题。

sentences.en: This is what makes humans so unique and different than any other species.
sentences.zh: 这正是人类区别于其他物种的独特之处。

sentences.en: But there are many other parts of our brains where work is happening quite outside of conscious awareness.
sentences.zh: 但我们大脑中还有许多其他部分，它们的工作完全是在潜意识层面进行的。

sentences.en: And that's a very smart way for a system to be.
sentences.zh: 对于一个系统来说，这是一种非常聪明的运作方式。

sentences.en: A simple computer, not anything like as complex or as magnificent as our brains, is doing a lot of work that's not visible to us on our monitors.
sentences.zh: 一台简单的计算机——远没有我们的大脑复杂或宏大——也在后台处理着许多我们显示器上看不见的工作。

sentences.en: It's churning out data.
sentences.zh: 它在处理数据。

sentences.en: It's putting things together.
sentences.zh: 它在整合信息。

sentences.en: It's updating stuff.
sentences.zh: 它在更新内容。

sentences.en: It's doing all of that work quite outside of our ability to visualize it.
sentences.zh: 它在完全超出我们可视化能力的情况下完成所有这些工作。

sentences.en: Why?
sentences.zh: 为什么？

sentences.en: That's what makes that computer smart.
sentences.zh: 这就是让计算机变得智能的原因。

sentences.en: It's doing a whole bunch more stuff, and it doesn't need to start everything up every single time.
sentences.zh: 它在做更多的事情，而且不需要每次都从头启动。

sentences.en: These are routines it has learned.
sentences.zh: 这些是它已经学会的例行程序。

sentences.en: We call them compiled programs that are set to deal with certain things that happen all the time.
sentences.zh: 我们称之为“编译程序”，它们被设定用来处理经常发生的特定事情。

sentences.en: We have those two.
sentences.zh: 我们也有这些程序。

sentences.en: And some of those compiled programs that we have and that we carry in our minds have the vestiges of the paSt. They are left inside of
sentences.zh: 我们大脑中携带的一些编译程序带有过去的残余。它们留在了

sentences.en: our heads and in the ways in which our brain works that come from a time and a place in our history where we lived with people who were just like us.
sentences.zh: 我们的脑海中，以及我们大脑运作的方式中，这些源于我们历史上某个时期和地点，那时我们只与和我们一样的人生活在一起。

sentences.en: They were genetically identical to us in our own little tribe of a 30 people, 150 people or whatever.
sentences.zh: 在我们的部落里，无论是30人还是150人，他们与我们在基因上是完全相同的。

sentences.en: On the other side of the mountain from which our ancestors lived was another group of people who maybe were different from us because they put a different
sentences.zh: 在我们祖先居住的山的那一边，有另一群人，他们可能与我们不同，因为他们会在脸上涂抹不同的

sentences.en: mark on their face or wore a different kind of clothing, but they were genetically also just the same as us.
sentences.zh: 标记或穿着不同类型的衣服，但在基因上他们和我们是一样的。

sentences.en: And yet when the two met, especially at some resource like food or water, and when it looked
sentences.zh: 然而，当双方相遇时，特别是在争夺食物或水等资源时，当看起来

sentences.en: like only one of us could have that resource, we learned that we had to do certain things, not very nice things to other people in order to survive.
sentences.zh: 只有一方能获得资源时，我们学会了为了生存必须做某些事情，对其他人做一些不太友好的事情。

sentences.en: Some of that has been left in our brains, even though our world has changed dramatically.
sentences.zh: 尽管我们的世界已经发生了翻天覆地的变化，但其中一些东西仍留在了我们的大脑中。

sentences.en: So I always argue that if we just go back to something that's attributed to Darwin, that it is not the strongest who will survive, nor the most intelligent, but the
sentences.zh: 所以我总是说，如果我们回到达尔文所归纳的观点，即生存下来的不是最强壮的，也不是最聪明的，而是

sentences.en: ones who are most adaptive to change.
sentences.zh: 最能适应变化的那些。

sentences.en: If we believe that, then what we're speaking about today is that kind of adaptation, because in the old world, perhaps it was reasonable, rational to be suspicious of
sentences.zh: 如果我们相信这一点，那么我们今天所谈论的就是那种适应性，因为在旧世界，对

sentences.en: people who looked very different from us.
sentences.zh: 看起来与我们非常不同的人保持警惕，或许是合理且理性的。

sentences.en: But today, the way our world is set up, it's the exact opposite that is being called for if we want to succeed, if we want to adapt.
sentences.zh: 但今天，按照我们世界的运作方式，如果我们想要成功，想要适应，恰恰需要反其道而行之。

sentences.en: And that is, if a business person looks at somebody very different from them, I think it would be worthwhile for that business person to
sentences.zh: 也就是说，如果一个商人看到一个与自己非常不同的人，我认为该商人值得去

sentences.en: say, how can I outsource to that person and make a lot of money for my business?
sentences.zh: 思考：我该如何与那个人外包合作，并为我的生意赚取大量利润？

sentences.en: So you see how our moment is calling for a very different kind of approach and a different kind of behavior than
sentences.zh: 所以你看，我们所处的时代要求一种与过去完全不同的方法和行为，

sentences.en: the one that paid off in the long paSt. And that is part of the reason why we fail, because not only is
sentences.zh: 那种在过去行之有效的方法。这也是我们失败的部分原因，因为这些东西不仅是隐形的，

sentences.en: the stuff invisible, it also the natural orientation would be towards similarity or familiarity and so on, which today is not necessarily going to be suited.
sentences.zh: 而且自然的倾向会偏向相似性或熟悉度等等，这在今天未必适用。

sentences.en: I have to go find people who know things I simply don't know, which means people from different fields, people from different cultures.
sentences.zh: 我必须去寻找那些拥有我所不具备知识的人，这意味着来自不同领域、不同文化的人。

sentences.en: So I have to do something that almost goes against my nature.
sentences.zh: 所以我必须做一些几乎违背我本性的事情。

sentences.en: Let me ask you how you got interested in this topic.
sentences.zh: 让我问问你是如何对这个话题产生兴趣的。

sentences.en: I understand that you began your career studying memory.
sentences.zh: 我了解到你职业生涯的起点是研究记忆。

sentences.en: So how did you move from memory to implicit attitudes and where where's the connection?
sentences.zh: 那么你是如何从记忆转向内隐态度的？这两者之间有什么联系？

sentences.en: So I'm one of those very fortunate people who came to be in a field at a time when clearly
sentences.zh: 我是那种非常幸运的人，在一个领域显然正在发生某些事情的时候进入了该领域。

sentences.en: something was happening.
sentences.zh: 其他人已经扫清了障碍，而我恰好站在巨人的肩膀上。

sentences.en: Other people had cleared the brush and I happened to stand on the shoulders of giants.
sentences.zh: 是的，我曾经对人类记忆感兴趣。

sentences.en: Yes, I was interested in human memory.
sentences.zh: 我对社会群体或偏见毫无兴趣。

sentences.en: I had zero interest in social groups or bias.
sentences.zh: 我当时并没有寻找关于那个课题的研究。

sentences.en: I wasn't looking for research to do on that topic.
sentences.zh: 但在研究记忆的过程中——这就是幸运的部分——人类记忆领域正在发生一场小小的革命。

sentences.en: But in the process of doing research on memory, and this is the fortunate part, a little revolution was happening in the field of human memory.
sentences.zh: 自19世纪末艾宾浩斯以来，研究记忆超过100年的人们一直使用一种测量方法。

sentences.en: People who had been studying memory for over 100 years since Ebbinghaus in the late 1800s were studying memory using one kind of measure.
sentences.zh: 我们会问人们：你今天早餐吃了什么？

sentences.en: We would ask people, what did you eat for breakfast today?
sentences.zh: 或者你五岁时发生了什么？

sentences.en: Or what happened to you when you were five years old?
sentences.zh: 或者你刚刚在实验室里学习了一串单词。

sentences.en: Or you just learned a list of words in the lab.
sentences.zh: 告诉我那些单词是什么。

sentences.en: Tell me what those words are.
sentences.zh: 无论内容如何不同，所有这些方法和问题相似之处在于单一的方法。

sentences.en: However different the content may be, what was similar to all these methods, all these questions was a single method.
sentences.zh: 那就是，这种方法要求我们——即记忆力正在被测试的人——进入自己的大脑，有意识地提取出某些东西。

sentences.en: And that is that the method required us, the human whose memory was being tested, to go into her mind and pull out something consciously.
sentences.zh: 因为你必须这样做才能回答这些问题。

sentences.en: Because you'd have to do that to answer those questions.
sentences.zh: 今天我们称这种记忆形式为“外显记忆”。

sentences.en: Today we call that form of memory explicit memory.
sentences.zh: 因为它需要一种明确的行动，需要有意识的觉知来进入我们的大脑，从过去提取某些东西。

sentences.en: Because it requires an explicit action that requires conscious awareness to go into our minds to pull out something from the paSt. What was happening at the time I came to graduate
sentences.zh: 在我20世纪80年代进入研究生院时，人们开始意识到我们可能还有另一种形式的记忆。

sentences.en: school in the 1980s is a recognition that there might be another form of memory that we had.
sentences.zh: 它根本不会对那样的问题做出反应。

sentences.en: That simply did not respond to questions like that.
sentences.zh: 这些数据来自失忆症患者。

sentences.en: These data came from amnesic patients.
sentences.zh: 这些数据甚至来自并非失忆症的普通人，表明确实有一些东西通过我们的经历被记录在

sentences.en: These data came even from ordinary people who were not amnesics, showing that there is stuff that gets laid down in our
sentences.zh: 大脑中，而我们可能对此毫无记忆。

sentences.en: brain through our experiences that we may have no recollection of.
sentences.zh: 然而，如果你使用正确的测试、正确的探测手段，你可能会发现它的证据。

sentences.en: And yet, if you use the right test, the right probe, you might find evidence for it.
sentences.zh: 因此，我记得挑选过一项研究，虽然不是完全随机，但也差不多，是在我们过去举办的记忆午餐会上展示的。

sentences.en: And so, one such study that I remember picking, not quite at random, but almost, to present in a brown bag on memory that we used to run.
sentences.zh: 我的同事，

sentences.en: My colleague,
sentences.zh: 研究听觉记忆的 Rob Crowder，以及我在耶鲁大学（我的第一份工作所在地）时，

sentences.en: Rob Crowder, who studied auditory memory, and I at Yale University, where my first job was,
sentences.zh: 我们组织了一个名为“记忆午餐小组”的小团体，在那里我们会讨论关于记忆的研究。

sentences.en: we ran a little group called the Memory Lunch Group, where we would talk about studies on memory.
sentences.zh: 我决定展示一位名叫 Larry Jacobi 的天才认知心理学家和他的同事们所做的一项研究。

sentences.en: And I decided to present a study done by a genius cognitive psychologist by the name of Larry Jacobi and his colleagues.
sentences.zh: Larry 所做的是向人们展示他从电话簿里找出的名字，比如 Sebastian Weisdorf 这样的名字。

sentences.en: And what Larry had done is shown people names that he had pulled out of a phone book, say, a name like Sebastian Weisdorf.
sentences.zh: 然后，读过电话簿上那些名字的人离开了，一两天后他们又回来了。

sentences.en: And then people who read those names from the phone book went away and then they came back a day or two later.
sentences.zh: 现在他给了他们一份新的名字列表。

sentences.en: And now he gave them a new list of names.
sentences.zh: 那份列表包含了他们之前见过的名字，比如 Sebastian Weisdorf，但也包括像 Timothy Watson 这样不是名人、但来自同一电话簿的新名字。

sentences.en: That list consisted of the names they had seen before, Sebastian Weisdorf, but also new names like Timothy Watson that were not famous names, but from the same phone book.
sentences.zh: 然后他在列表中加入了一些名人的名字。

sentences.en: And then he added into that list names of some famous people.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: Wayne Gretzky 在当时就是这样一个名字，他是著名的加拿大冰球运动员，还有运动员、电影明星、摇滚音乐家等名字，无论是什么。

sentences.en: Wayne Gretzky was such a name at the time he was known, a famous Canadian hockey players, names of athletes, names of film stars, rock musicians, whatever it was.
sentences.zh: 现在，想象你是这项研究的受试者。

sentences.en: Now, imagine you're the subject in this study.
sentences.zh: 你在第一天来的时候看到了一些名字，然后离开了，现在你又回来了。

sentences.en: You came on day one and you saw some names and you went away and now you've come back.
sentences.zh: 在你面前是一份名字列表。

sentences.en: And before you is a list of names.
sentences.zh: 这些研究是用纸笔完成的。

sentences.en: These studies were done with paper and pencil.
sentences.zh: 这是一份很长的名字列表。

sentences.en: And these, this is a long list of names.
sentences.zh: 它包含一些旧名字、一些新名字，都不是名人的，然后混入了一些名人的名字。

sentences.en: It has some old names, some new names, all not famous, and then mixed in with some famous names.
sentences.zh: 任务非常简单。

sentences.en: And the task was very simple.
sentences.zh: 这就是我喜欢这个实验的地方。

sentences.en: This is what I loved about the experiment.
sentences.zh: Larry 对受试者说，你们知道，只需看每个名字，然后回答是或否。

sentences.en: Larry said to the subjects and his, you know, just look at each name and just say yes or no.
sentences.zh: 这是名人的名字吗？

sentences.en: Is this the name of a famous person or not?
sentences.zh: 所以如果人们准确回答，他们应该说 Wayne Gretzky 是名人，而 Timothy

sentences.en: So if people were to respond accurately, they should say Wayne Gretzky, yes, famous, but Timothy
sentences.zh: Watson 和 Sebastian Weisdorf 不是名人。

sentences.en: Watson and Sebastian Weisdorf, not famous.
sentences.zh: 但情况并非如此。

sentences.en: But that didn't happen.
sentences.zh: 他展示的是，确实，

sentences.en: What he showed is that indeed,
sentences.zh: Timothy Watson 被正确地识别为非名人。

sentences.en: Timothy Watson was identified as not famous correctly.
sentences.zh: 但现在想想 Sebastian Weisdorf，一个你前一天见过的名字，再次出现时，它具有一种他称之为“知觉流畅性”的特质。

sentences.en: But now think about Sebastian Weisdorf, a name you saw the day before, appears again, and it has a quality that he called perceptual fluency.
sentences.zh: 当你读到 Sebastian Weisdorf 这个名字时，你会觉得它很熟悉。

sentences.en: When you read the name Sebastian Weisdorf, it looks familiar to you.
sentences.zh: 但你的大脑并不记得 Sebastian Weisdorf 现在是一位足球运动员、摇滚明星，还是你前一天见过的名字。

sentences.en: But your brain doesn't remember whether Sebastian Weisdorf is now a football player or a rock star or a name you saw the day before.
sentences.zh: （注：此条对应原稿中第149条，已翻译）

sentences.en: This becomes confusing.
sentences.zh: 这变得令人困惑。

sentences.en: And in that moment, implicit memory kicks in and people wrongly identify
sentences.zh: 在那一刻，内隐记忆开始发挥作用，人们会错误地将

sentences.en: Sebastian Weisdorf as famous.
sentences.zh: 塞巴斯蒂安·魏斯多夫（Sebastian Weisdorf）认定为名人。

sentences.en: He called this result becoming famous overnight by just showing that, you know, when things are not consciously, if you were consciously able to recognize that Sebastian

sentences.en: Weisdorf was a name you saw two days ago, I think you would legitimately reject it as a famous name.

sentences.en: But because we've forgotten and especially forgotten time information, place information, where did this happen?
sentences.zh: 但因为我们遗忘了，特别是遗忘了时间信息、地点信息，比如这事发生在什么时候？

sentences.en: When did this happen?
sentences.zh: 这事是什么时候发生的？

sentences.en: Then the rest of the stuff starts to look familiar, and you use that as the basis of this incorrect judgment.
sentences.zh: 那么剩下的东西就开始显得熟悉了，而你把这当作做出错误判断的基础。

sentences.en: I was, I just thought this was a very cool study.
sentences.zh: 我当时……我只是觉得这是一项非常酷的研究。

sentences.en: And I decided to write to Jacoby and get the materials for the study to replicate them.
sentences.zh: 我决定写信给雅各比（Jacoby），获取这项研究的资料来复现它们。

sentences.en: And this is in 1989, because his study appeared in my basic.
sentences.zh: 那是在1989年，因为他的研究出现在我的基础研究中。

sentences.en: And I assume for the material, as we did in those old days, we used to actually have little postcards that we had printed up.
sentences.zh: 我假设对于这些资料，就像我们过去常做的那样，我们实际上会用印好的小明信片。

sentences.en: And that we would fill in the name of the article and write the address of the person and put it in
sentences.zh: 我们会填上文章的名字，写上收件人的地址，然后把它放进

sentences.en: US mail.
sentences.zh: 美国邮政。

sentences.en: And then you would wait, you would check your physical mailbox every day because you are expecting a big fat manila envelope.
sentences.zh: 然后你就会等待，你每天都会检查你的实体邮箱，因为你在期待一个厚厚的马尼拉纸信封。

sentences.en: And one arrived with all of the materials that Professor Jacoby generously sent to me.
sentences.zh: 后来，雅各比教授慷慨地寄给我的所有资料都到了。

sentences.en: As I looked at the materials, I noticed that all the names, you know, famous and not famous were male men's names.
sentences.zh: 当我查看这些资料时，我注意到所有的名字，你知道，无论是名人的还是非名人的，都是男性的名字。

sentences.en: And as I tell the story, you know, I wrote him another postcard, like, Dr. Jacoby, you only sent me half your stimuli, where the other half, I didn't actually do that.
sentences.zh: 正如我讲的那个故事，你知道，我又给他写了一张明信片，写着：“雅各比博士，你只寄给我了一半的刺激材料，另一半在哪儿？”其实我没真的那么做。

sentences.en: I did talk to him about it though.
sentences.zh: 不过我确实和他谈过这件事。

sentences.en: And he said, but women are not famous.
sentences.zh: 他说：“但女性不是名人啊。”

sentences.en: And if we, you know, it just, and you know, when he said that to me, it made complete sense.
sentences.zh: 如果我们，你知道，这只是……当你听到他对我那么说时，这完全讲得通。

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: Like if you want to do a psychological study, you would have to on memory, which is not on gender.
sentences.zh: 就像如果你想做一个心理学研究，你必须针对记忆，而不是针对性别。

sentences.en: The question was, why would you bother to get equal because now you'd have to get equal numbers of famous males and females.
sentences.zh: 问题是，你为什么要费心去追求平等呢？因为现在你必须获得等量的男性和女性名人名字。

sentences.en: It's just not relevant to the study.
sentences.zh: 这与研究无关。

sentences.en: So often in research, we take that path of finding the most, the best stimuli.
sentences.zh: 所以在研究中，我们经常走那条寻找最合适、最好的刺激材料的道路。

sentences.en: And the best stimuli in this case would have been to keep everything constant to use just men's names.
sentences.zh: 在这种情况下，最好的刺激材料就是保持一切不变，只使用男性的名字。

sentences.en: Now I understood that, but this is what I'd love your listeners to think about.
sentences.zh: 现在我理解了这一点，但这正是我希望你们的听众思考的问题。

sentences.en: Something made me spend an entire summer coming up with equally famous.
sentences.zh: 某种东西促使我花了一整个夏天的时间来构思同样出名的名字。

sentences.en: I tried equally famous men and women's names.
sentences.zh: 我尝试了同样出名的男性和女性名字。

sentences.en: I was not successful in coming up with equally famous men's and women's names, but I did that.
sentences.zh: 我在构思同样出名的男性和女性名字方面并不成功，但我确实做了。

sentences.en: You know, I went to books and I looked at, you know, nothing on the internet, of course.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我查阅了书籍，我看了，你知道，当然那时还没有互联网。

sentences.en: So it was hard to do, but I would test small groups of people and try to come up with names, you know, like Jane Austen or whatever, so that many people would recognize.
sentences.zh: 所以这很难做到，但我会测试一小群人，试着想出一些名字，你知道，比如简·奥斯汀（Jane Austen）之类的，这样很多人都会认出来。

sentences.en: And so I just did what I thought was a replication of the Jacobi study, but just with both kinds of
sentences.zh: 所以我只是做了我认为是雅各比研究的复现，但其中包含了两种

sentences.en: names in it, expecting of course, full well, that the same results should happen for male names and female names.
sentences.zh: 名字，当然，我完全预期男性名字和女性名字应该会产生同样的结果。

sentences.en: Why should that be different?
sentences.zh: 为什么会有所不同呢？

sentences.en: Once you had become familiar with a name like Sally
sentences.zh: 一旦你熟悉了像莎莉（Sally）

sentences.en: Weisdorf, you should now be more likely to say Sally Weisdorf was famous, just like you did for
sentences.zh: 魏斯多夫这样的名字，你现在应该更有可能说莎莉·魏斯多夫是名人，就像你对

sentences.en: Sebastian Weisdorf.
sentences.zh: 塞巴斯蒂安·魏斯多夫所做的那样。

sentences.en: But in six experiments, that's not what I found.
sentences.zh: 但在六项实验中，我发现的并不是这样。

sentences.en: I was surprised.
sentences.zh: 我很惊讶。

sentences.en: Initially, I just thought it was a throwaway result and I would just let it go and say, you know, the women's names did not become famous overnight the way the men's names did.
sentences.zh: 起初，我只是认为这是一个无关紧要的结果，我打算就此作罢，说，你知道，女性名字并没有像男性名字那样“一夜成名”。

sentences.en: But as I thought about it, I began to quiz my subjects.
sentences.zh: 但当我思考这个问题时，我开始询问我的受试者。

sentences.en: I used to run my own experiments.
sentences.zh: 我过去常自己进行实验。

sentences.en: In those days, I ran every single subject and I would say to them at the end of the study, so what do you think you used as the rule to identify fame?
sentences.zh: 在那些日子里，我亲自测试每一个受试者，在研究结束时我会问他们：“那么，你认为你用了什么规则来判断名气？”

sentences.en: Not one of them said the gender of the name.
sentences.zh: 没有一个人说是名字的性别。

sentences.en: So then I started to say to them, do you think you might have used the gender of the name in making your decision?
sentences.zh: 于是我开始问他们：“你认为你在做决定时是否可能使用了名字的性别？”

sentences.en: And they would look surprised and sometimes even offended.
sentences.zh: 他们会显得很惊讶，有时甚至感到被冒犯。

sentences.en: Well, what do you think?
sentences.zh: 嗯，你觉得呢？

sentences.en: I am a sexiSt. You know, of course, I wasn't using the gender of the name.
sentences.zh: “我是个性别歧视者吗？”你知道，当然，我并没有使用名字的性别。

sentences.en: And yet that was so clearly in the data.
sentences.zh: 然而这在数据中却表现得如此明显。

sentences.en: I did a presentation at a conference in which I think I took the bold step of saying, I've quizzed, you know, 400 subjects about this.
sentences.zh: 我在一次会议上做了一个演讲，我想我采取了一个大胆的步骤，我说：“我已经询问了，你知道，400名受试者关于这个问题。”

sentences.en: Not one of them was aware that he or she was using the gender of the name to decide on the person's likelihood of fame.
sentences.zh: 没有一个人意识到他或她在利用名字的性别来判断一个人的名气可能性。

sentences.en: And yet in their data, we saw this.
sentences.zh: 然而在他们的数据中，我们看到了这一点。

sentences.en: If this is true, then harm is happening without the person doing the harm being aware that they're doing it.
sentences.zh: 如果这是真的，那么伤害就在发生，而实施伤害的人并没有意识到他们在这样做。

sentences.en: The person being harmed is not going to be aware that she was harmed.
sentences.zh: 受到伤害的人也不会意识到她受到了伤害。

sentences.en: What does this mean for the big question of how we're going to treat each other in a democratic
sentences.zh: 对于我们如何在民主社会中对待彼此这一重大问题，这意味着什么？

sentences.en: society where we believe that fairness and egalitarianism and so on are the virtues we care about?
sentences.zh: 在一个我们相信公平、平等主义等是我们所珍视的美德的社会中？

sentences.en: And that's where it started.
sentences.zh: 这就是一切的开始。

sentences.en: That's pretty amazing.
sentences.zh: 这太令人惊叹了。

sentences.en: Well, one of the best known ways today to test implicit bias is through something you were involved in creating, the implicit association teSt.
sentences.zh: 嗯，今天测试内隐偏见最著名的方法之一是通过你参与创建的“内隐联想测验”（IAT）。

sentences.en: How did that come about?
sentences.zh: 这是怎么产生的？

sentences.en: How does that test work?
sentences.zh: 这个测验是如何运作的？

sentences.en: So the credit here goes to my colleague,
sentences.zh: 所以，功劳归于我的同事，

sentences.en: Tony Greenwald, who, again, I think even he didn't come to it with an interest in creating something that
sentences.zh: 托尼·格林沃尔德（Tony Greenwald），我想即使是他，最初也不是带着创造出

sentences.en: became the IAT, he was really dissatisfied with the methods that we were using at the time to get at implicit bias that weren't really that powerful.
sentences.zh: 后来成为IAT的东西的兴趣来的，他真的对我们当时用来获取内隐偏见的方法感到不满，因为那些方法并不那么强大。

sentences.en: We would get differences and you can't do, you know, one fame study after another is the way to study implicit bias.
sentences.zh: 我们会得到差异，但你不能，你知道，一个接一个地做名气研究来研究内隐偏见。

sentences.en: Something more general was needed.
sentences.zh: 需要更通用的东西。

sentences.en: We did have a method in psychology.
sentences.zh: 我们在心理学中确实有一种方法。

sentences.en: It's called semantic priming.
sentences.zh: 它被称为语义启动。

sentences.en: If I flash a word rapidly on a computer screen and the word is something like soldier, let's say, if the word that follows it is John,
sentences.zh: 如果我在电脑屏幕上快速闪过一个词，比如“士兵”，假设紧随其后的词是“约翰”（John），

sentences.en: you'll be much more quickly able to identify John than if the word is Jane, because soldier and John go
sentences.zh: 你会比词是“简”（Jane）时更快地识别出约翰，因为士兵和约翰在我们的记忆、头脑和理解中是

sentences.en: together in our memory and in our minds and our understanding rather than soldier and Jane.
sentences.zh: 联系在一起的，而不是士兵和简。

sentences.en: And likewise, you know, if I said something like nurse and John, you'd be slower to respond to John after nurse than you would be to Jane.
sentences.zh: 同样地，你知道，如果我说“护士”和“约翰”，你在护士之后对约翰的反应会比对简慢。

sentences.en: So that was a method.
sentences.zh: 所以那是一种方法。

sentences.en: I was using that method.
sentences.zh: 我当时正在使用那种方法。

sentences.en: It was producing good data, but it was inefficient.
sentences.zh: 它产生了很好的数据，但效率低下。

sentences.en: You know, you would need to give people 800 trials.
sentences.zh: 你知道，你需要给人们做800次试验。

sentences.en: Imagine a poor subject sitting at a computer, you know, 800 times having to answer these questions and for a whole hour.
sentences.zh: 想象一个可怜的受试者坐在电脑前，你知道，800次必须回答这些问题，持续整整一个小时。

sentences.en: And then the effect size was small.
sentences.zh: 而且效应量很小。

sentences.en: It was always there.
sentences.zh: 它总是存在的。

sentences.en: So for the scientists doing research on understanding the human mind, it was perfectly okay.
sentences.zh: 所以对于研究人类思维的科学家来说，这完全没问题。

sentences.en: But you, the subject, if you were taking that test, you wouldn't necessarily have the feeling or the experience that you were showing a bias.
sentences.zh: 但你，作为受试者，如果你参加那个测试，你不一定会感觉到或体验到你表现出了偏见。

sentences.en: And what Tony Greenwald did is tried the slightly different way of trying to get at the strength of association between A and D in our minds.
sentences.zh: 托尼·格林沃尔德所做的是尝试了一种稍微不同的方法，试图找出我们头脑中A和D之间联想的强度。

sentences.en: The way the IAT or the implicit association test works is actually quite simple.
sentences.zh: IAT或内隐联想测验的工作方式其实很简单。

sentences.en: It makes the assumption that if two things have co-occurred in our experience over and over again, then we'll put those two things together very quickly.
sentences.zh: 它基于这样一个假设：如果两件事在我们的经验中反复共同出现，那么我们就会非常快地把这两件事联系在一起。

sentences.en: Salt and pepper is just a simple example, okay?
sentences.zh: 盐和胡椒就是一个简单的例子，对吧？

sentences.en: Bacon and eggs, if you want to stay with food-related things.
sentences.zh: 培根和鸡蛋，如果你想用食物相关的例子的话。

sentences.en: But mother and father, or father and he, mother and she, these are things that have co-occurred in our mind, in our experience, and therefore they have a strong connection.
sentences.zh: 但母亲和父亲，或者父亲和“他”，母亲和“她”，这些是在我们的头脑、我们的经验中共同出现的事物，因此它们有很强的联系。

sentences.en: Neuroscientists have a little phrase that they use to teach people about learning of that kind, and their phrase is a very useful one.
sentences.zh: 神经科学家有一个小短语，他们用它来教人们关于那种学习方式，他们的短语非常有用。

sentences.en: When they speak about neurons, they say, what fires together, wires together.
sentences.zh: 当他们谈论神经元时，他们说：“一起激发的，就会连接在一起。”

sentences.en: And that's what we are trying to get at.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们试图要达到的目标。

sentences.en: We know that some things have fired together.
sentences.zh: 我们知道有些事物已经一起激发了。

sentences.en: Can we build a method that will give us an indication of how strongly they're wired together?
sentences.zh: 我们能建立一种方法来指示它们连接得有多紧密吗？

sentences.en: And so the IAT works in a very simple way.
sentences.zh: 所以IAT的工作方式非常简单。

sentences.en: It requires you, and I would say to your listeners, there is no way in which you will appreciate the IAT by listening
sentences.zh: 它要求你，我会对你的听众说，你不可能通过听我所说的来理解IAT，就像你亲自参加一次测验那样。

sentences.en: to what I say as much as you will by taking a teSt. Right, which anyone can do, and we'll include a link in the show notes.
sentences.zh: 没错，任何人都可以做，我们会在节目说明中附上链接。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So, so what happens in an IAT, and let's just take something like gender and work.
sentences.zh: 那么，在IAT中会发生什么，让我们以性别和工作为例。

sentences.en: In our experience, even though women have entered the workforce in very large numbers, in our
sentences.zh: 在我们的经验中，尽管女性已经大量进入职场，但在我们的

sentences.en: minds, male and career, to the extent that they're more closely associated, should get picked up on a test like the following.
sentences.zh: 头脑中，男性和职业，就它们联系得更紧密的程度而言，应该会在像下面这样的测试中被捕捉到。

sentences.en: You see names of men and women, a name like Peter may show up, a name like Susan may show up, you're told use two keys on your keyboard.
sentences.zh: 你看到男性和女性的名字，比如彼得（Peter）可能会出现，苏珊（Susan）可能会出现，你被告知使用键盘上的两个键。

sentences.en: If you see a male name, press the left key.
sentences.zh: 如果你看到一个男性名字，按左键。

sentences.en: If you see a female name, press the right key.
sentences.zh: 如果你看到一个女性名字，按右键。

sentences.en: So easy to do.
sentences.zh: 这很容易做到。

sentences.en: Now we say, okay, we're going to now give you words that mean home and career words.
sentences.zh: 现在我们说，好的，我们现在要给你一些代表家庭和职业的词。

sentences.en: If you see a work like child or marriage or garden or kitchen, you will press, you know, the right key.
sentences.zh: 如果你看到一个像“孩子”、“婚姻”、“花园”或“厨房”这样的词，你会按，你知道，右键。

sentences.en: If you see a career word, a word like office, manager, job, briefcase, desk, things like that, you will press the left key.
sentences.zh: 如果你看到一个职业词，像“办公室”、“经理”、“工作”、“公文包”、“书桌”之类的词，你会按左键。

sentences.en: And now what you do in the IAT, and this is the critical moment, you combine them.
sentences.zh: 现在你在IAT中所做的，这是关键时刻，你把它们结合起来。

sentences.en: So you say, all right, you're going to see all four kinds of things, male, female, home, career.
sentences.zh: 所以你说，好吧，你将看到所有四种类型的东西：男性、女性、家庭、职业。

sentences.en: For now, if it's a male name like Peter, or a office related word like boardroom or briefcase, press the left key.
sentences.zh: 现在，如果是像彼得这样的男性名字，或者像“董事会”或“公文包”这样与办公室相关的词，按左键。

sentences.en: So you're putting those two together.
sentences.zh: 所以你把这两者放在一起。

sentences.en: If it's a female name like Susan, or a word like kitchen from, from home, you press the right key.
sentences.zh: 如果是像苏珊这样的女性名字，或者像“厨房”这样来自家庭的词，你按右键。

sentences.en: It's very easy for us to do that, because that set of trials is picking up what we think of as the established stereotypical association.
sentences.zh: 我们很容易做到这一点，因为那组试验捕捉到了我们认为是既定的刻板印象联想。

sentences.en: So if you're taking a test when you have to do that, you're whizzing through it, you're making very few mistakes, and your speed to
sentences.zh: 所以如果你在参加测试时必须这样做，你会飞快地完成它，几乎不会犯错，而且你的反应速度，

sentences.en: response, which is our critical measure time to respond, call a response latency in milliseconds.
sentences.zh: 这是我们的关键测量指标——反应时间，以毫秒为单位的反应潜伏期。

sentences.en: But what happens unbeknownst to you, you're now told, okay, you did very well.
sentences.zh: 但接下来发生的事情是你不知道的，你现在被告知：“好的，你做得很好。”

sentences.en: Now let's get you to do something a little different.
sentences.zh: “现在让我们让你做点不同的事情。”

sentences.en: Now, put Peter and kitchen together, and put Susan and boardroom together using these keys on the keyboard.
sentences.zh: “现在，把彼得和厨房放在一起，把苏珊和董事会放在一起，使用键盘上的这些键。”

sentences.en: Very simple.
sentences.zh: 非常简单。

sentences.en: And everybody thinks, oh, I should be able to do that.
sentences.zh: 每个人都想，哦，我应该能做到这一点。

sentences.en: Nobody thinks that they can't do that.
sentences.zh: 没人认为他们做不到。

sentences.en: I should be able to imagine Peter in the kitchen,
sentences.zh: 我应该能想象彼得在厨房里，

sentences.en: Susan and, you know, in a boardroom, no problem, until you start to do it.
sentences.zh: 苏珊在董事会里，没问题，直到你开始做的时候。

sentences.en: And so people like me, who have always had a career, I was born and raised in South India.
sentences.zh: 所以像我这样一直有职业生涯的人，我在印度南部出生长大。

sentences.en: My mother, in a society where women didn't work outside the home, did, and was a teacher.
sentences.zh: 我的母亲，在一个女性不在家外工作的社会里，她工作了，而且是一名教师。

sentences.en: In spite of all of these direct personal experiences, I can't do this.
sentences.zh: 尽管有所有这些直接的个人经历，我还是做不到。

sentences.en: I can't do it as fast as I could do the previous version.
sentences.zh: 我无法像做上一个版本那样快地完成它。

sentences.en: And when, you know, so when after those Jacoby experiments that I had done earlier, you know, we had to come up with a name for this thing.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，在那些我早先做过的雅各比实验之后，我们必须为这个东西想个名字。

sentences.en: And we were struggling with the name.
sentences.zh: 我们一直在为名字而挣扎。

sentences.en: And because I'd been studying memory, and the phrase that they were using was implicit memory, to distinguish it from conscious or explicit
sentences.zh: 因为我一直在研究记忆，他们使用的短语是“内隐记忆”，以区别于有意识或外显记忆，

sentences.en: memory, we called this implicit bias, because it was now showing a ability to do one thing faster
sentences.zh: 我们称之为“内隐偏见”，因为它现在显示出一种做一件事比做另一件事更快的能力，

sentences.en: than the other, as a measure of what I call the thumbprint of the culture on our brain.
sentences.zh: 作为我所说的“文化在我们大脑上的指纹”的一种衡量标准。

sentences.en: That's not always consistent with your view of yourself.
sentences.zh: 这并不总是与你对自己的看法一致。

sentences.en: And that's the dissociation.
sentences.zh: 这就是解离。

sentences.en: So in psychology, the term dissociation is an important one, when in this case, it's where your data on one measure, when I explicitly ask you, you'll say one thing,
sentences.zh: 所以在心理学中，解离这个术语很重要，在这种情况下，它是指你在一个指标上的数据——当我明确问你时，你会说一件事，

sentences.en: but on then the implicit measure, something different is showing up.
sentences.zh: 但在内隐指标上，却显示出不同的东西。

sentences.en: So I show no bias.
sentences.zh: 所以我表现出没有偏见。

sentences.en: If you ask me a survey question about who belongs more at home and who belongs more in the workplace, I will tell you equally men and women.
sentences.zh: 如果你问我一个关于谁更应该待在家里、谁更应该待在职场的调查问题，我会告诉你男性和女性平等。

sentences.en: And then you give me this test, and it's not anything close to equal.
sentences.zh: 然后你给我做这个测试，结果一点也不平等。

sentences.en: I'm just unable to do it.
sentences.zh: 我只是做不到。

sentences.en: And we believe the test picks up the thumbprint of the culture on our brain.
sentences.zh: 我们相信这个测试捕捉到了文化在我们大脑上的指纹。

sentences.en: So is it possible to learn to overcome these implicit biases?
sentences.zh: 那么，有可能学会克服这些内隐偏见吗？

sentences.en: So you train yourself out of responding in that way.
sentences.zh: 所以你训练自己不再以那种方式做出反应。

sentences.en: And when you take the test, it doesn't show up that way anymore.
sentences.zh: 当你参加测试时，它就不会再以那种方式显示出来了。

sentences.en: You're actually able to relate things that wouldn't normally be related because you've done something to rewire your brain.
sentences.zh: 你实际上能够将通常不会相关的事物联系起来，因为你已经做了一些事情来重塑你的大脑。

sentences.en: Is that possible?
sentences.zh: 这可能吗？

sentences.en: Well, the best way to answer that question is to say, of course, of course, it can be changed because it was learned.
sentences.zh: 嗯，回答这个问题的最好方法是说，当然，当然，它可以改变，因为它是学来的。

sentences.en: So you could make yourself unlearn it.
sentences.zh: 所以你可以让自己“反学习”它。

sentences.en: But the mistake that people make is to think that they can unlearn it easily.
sentences.zh: 但人们犯的错误是认为他们可以轻易地反学习它。

sentences.en: Right?
sentences.zh: 对吧？

sentences.en: You think to yourself, okay, first, I don't want to believe that I have bias.
sentences.zh: 你会心想，好吧，首先，我不愿相信自己有偏见。

sentences.en: That's the first sort of defense.
sentences.zh: 这是第一种防御机制。

sentences.en: So you argue and you argue and you argue until you have been hemmed into a box from which you can't escape.
sentences.zh: 所以你会不断地争辩，直到把自己逼进一个无法逃脱的死胡同。

sentences.en: That shows you that that bias does exist in your head.
sentences.zh: 这说明你的脑子里确实存在那种偏见。

sentences.en: So then you agree.
sentences.zh: 于是你同意了。

sentences.en: And then you say, oh, but I'll just tell myself not to be that way.
sentences.zh: 然后你说，哦，但我会告诉自己不要那样做。

sentences.en: And that's the mistake.
sentences.zh: 而这就是错误所在。

sentences.en: So we should be aware.
sentences.zh: 所以我们应该保持警惕。

sentences.en: So there are many experiments that have been done in my lab recently, but in many other people's labs, where we try to look at what is
sentences.zh: 最近我的实验室以及许多其他人的实验室做了很多实验，我们试图观察究竟是什么

sentences.en: it that will change an existing implicit bias.
sentences.zh: 能够改变现有的内隐偏见。

sentences.en: The work of Calvin Lai at Washington University is very important here because he set these experiments up as a competition.
sentences.zh: 华盛顿大学 Calvin Lai 的研究在这里非常重要，因为他把这些实验设计成了一场竞赛。

sentences.en: You, if you were a scientist interested in this question, you could submit what you think is your best intervention to change data on the IAT.
sentences.zh: 如果你是一位对这个问题感兴趣的科学家，你可以提交你认为能改变 IAT（内隐联想测验）数据的最佳干预方案。

sentences.en: I won't go into the details.
sentences.zh: 细节我就不赘述了。

sentences.en: It's a long, laborious way to take all these people's ideas and turn it into a proper experiment where every intervention gets a fair shot at changing people's minds.
sentences.zh: 要把所有人的想法转化为一个正规的实验，让每种干预措施都有公平的机会去改变人们的想法，这是一个漫长而艰苦的过程。

sentences.en: Uh, he did it with race.
sentences.zh: 呃，他针对种族偏见做了这个实验。

sentences.en: So we can begin with the race IAT where 70% of white people and even
sentences.zh: 我们可以从种族 IAT 开始，70% 的白人甚至

sentences.en: Asians associate white with good and black with bad.
sentences.zh: 亚裔都将白人与“好”联系在一起，将黑人与“坏”联系在一起。

sentences.en: Um, you can begin with something like that.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你可以从类似这样的测试开始。

sentences.en: And then he asked people come up with a, you know, a certain minutes, I forget how long, but your intervention can't be long, longer than a few minutes.
sentences.zh: 然后他让人们想出一个，你知道，在一定时间内，我忘了具体多久，但你的干预措施不能太长，不能超过几分钟。

sentences.en: Uh, what, what do you think would work?
sentences.zh: 呃，你，你觉得什么会有效？

sentences.en: And it's a lovely way to do science because you're not prejudging what will work and what will not work.
sentences.zh: 这是一种做科学研究的绝佳方式，因为你没有预先判断什么有效，什么无效。

sentences.en: You get to, if you put the work into building that kind of experiment, he'll load it up on the website
sentences.zh: 如果你投入精力去构建那样的实验，他会把它上传到网站上，

sentences.en: and get data on it and tell all of us which ones worked and which ones didn't.
sentences.zh: 收集数据，然后告诉我们所有人哪些有效，哪些无效。

sentences.en: And a paper was published with many authors, um, to show which ones worked and which ones didn't.
sentences.zh: 后来发表了一篇有多位作者参与的论文，嗯，展示了哪些有效，哪些无效。

sentences.en: So interventions that he tried came in three different categories.
sentences.zh: 他尝试的干预措施分为三大类。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Intervention number one, you tell the subject, try to be egalitarian.
sentences.zh: 第一种干预措施，你告诉受试者，试着保持平等主义。

sentences.en: Do not be biased.
sentences.zh: 不要有偏见。

sentences.en: Try to treat these two groups equally.
sentences.zh: 试着平等对待这两个群体。

sentences.en: The second is you don't say anything to them, but you just give them new associations.
sentences.zh: 第二种是你什么都不对他们说，只是给他们新的联想。

sentences.en: So you pair black with good things, white with not so good things to see if that will just shift the IAT bias away from the default in our
sentences.zh: 所以你把黑人与好的事物配对，把白人与不太好的事物配对，看看这是否能将 IAT 偏见从我们

sentences.en: society and towards whatever you've just taught people.
sentences.zh: 社会默认的状态中转移出来，转向你刚刚教给人们的内容。

sentences.en: If that works, then that tells us that even implicit biases are open to intervention and to change.
sentences.zh: 如果这有效，那就说明即使是内隐偏见也可以通过干预来改变。

sentences.en: So that's number two, I call that sort of the associative measure method, or kind of like a brute force method.
sentences.zh: 所以这是第二种，我称之为联想测量法，或者说是一种蛮力法。

sentences.en: We're just going to give you new, new associations to see if they will replace the old ones.
sentences.zh: 我们只是要给你新的联想，看看它们是否能取代旧的。

sentences.en: And the third intervention is something that I think only humans can do.
sentences.zh: 第三种干预措施是我认为只有人类才能做到的。

sentences.en: You know, we can take any other animal other than us, take non-human animals and give them new associations and they'll learn those as we would.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们可以把除了我们以外的任何动物，把非人类动物拿来给它们新的联想，它们会像我们一样学习这些联想。

sentences.en: But there is something unique to humans and that's language and the ability to be able to soar in our minds and think entirely new thoughts.
sentences.zh: 但人类有一种独特的东西，那就是语言，以及在脑海中翱翔并产生全新思想的能力。

sentences.en: And so the third kind of intervention is one where you are asked to imagine, imagine a world in which you're suffering in some way and a person from group A, black,
sentences.zh: 所以第三种干预方式是让你想象，想象一个你正以某种方式受苦的世界，而一个来自 A 组（黑人）的人，

sentences.en: helps you, while a person from group B, white, does not help you.
sentences.zh: 帮助了你，而一个来自 B 组（白人）的人没有帮助你。

sentences.en: Okay?
sentences.zh: 好吗？

sentences.en: So you imagine that.
sentences.zh: 所以你想象那个场景。

sentences.en: Does that matter?
sentences.zh: 那有关系吗？

sentences.en: And the data show that what works is exactly in the opposite order of the way I gave you the three categories.
sentences.zh: 数据表明，有效的方法恰好与我给出的三类方法的顺序相反。

sentences.en: If you use that kind of linguistically based thinking, imagining somebody helps you, that produces the biggest change on the IAT.
sentences.zh: 如果你使用那种基于语言的思维，想象有人帮助你，那会在 IAT 上产生最大的改变。

sentences.en: You actually begin to become more pro-black than you were before or less empty black than you were before.
sentences.zh: 你实际上开始变得比以前更亲黑人，或者说比以前对黑人的负面偏见更少。

sentences.en: The second method, the associations, they work, but not as powerfully.
sentences.zh: 第二种方法，即联想，它们有效，但效果没那么强。

sentences.en: Okay?
sentences.zh: 好吗？

sentences.en: And this was a surprise to us because I had been thinking that that one would work the beSt. The IAT is measuring associations.
sentences.zh: 这让我们感到惊讶，因为我一直认为那一种会效果最好。IAT 测量的是联想。

sentences.en: We're messing directly with the association.
sentences.zh: 我们直接干预了联想。

sentences.en: So that should produce the biggest effect.
sentences.zh: 所以那应该产生最大的效果。

sentences.en: It does not.
sentences.zh: 但事实并非如此。

sentences.en: This is why I love science, you know, that every day I can make a hypothesis and one of my students will show me I'm wrong.
sentences.zh: 这就是我热爱科学的原因，你知道，每天我都可以提出一个假设，然后我的学生会向我证明我是错的。

sentences.en: And now we know something.
sentences.zh: 现在我们知道了些什么。

sentences.en: We know something new and better.
sentences.zh: 我们知道了新的、更好的东西。

sentences.en: And the worst method, the one that actually has no effect at all, is to tell people to be good people, to be egalitarian, and so on.
sentences.zh: 而最差的方法，那种实际上完全没有效果的方法，就是告诉人们要做个好人，要平等主义等等。

sentences.en: Okay?
sentences.zh: 好吗？

sentences.en: So let me say that this may make it sound like, oh, so it's easy to change.
sentences.zh: 所以让我说，这听起来可能像是，哦，原来改变很容易。

sentences.en: It is easy in the sense that it'll last for a short period of time, but it won't last very long.
sentences.zh: 从它能持续一小段时间的意义上来说，它确实很容易，但它不会持续太久。

sentences.en: You step out of that experiment and you enter the real world.
sentences.zh: 你走出那个实验，进入现实世界。

sentences.en: And the real world is again giving you data that make the same old, same old association between black and bad, white and good.
sentences.zh: 而现实世界又在给你提供数据，让你产生同样老掉牙的联想：黑人与坏，白人与好。

sentences.en: And so your brain snaps back.
sentences.zh: 于是你的大脑又弹回去了。

sentences.en: Now, when young people encounter this result, when they see that, yes, they were able to make change,
sentences.zh: 现在，当年轻人遇到这个结果时，当他们看到，是的，他们确实能够做出改变，

sentences.en: but the change doesn't last, they get very sad because they want a better world.
sentences.zh: 但改变无法持久，他们会感到非常难过，因为他们想要一个更好的世界。

sentences.en: And I'm not at all sad about that.
sentences.zh: 而我对此一点也不难过。

sentences.en: I think it's telling us the exact truth about how the human mind works.
sentences.zh: 我认为这恰恰告诉了我们人类思维运作的真相。

sentences.en: Can you imagine this?
sentences.zh: 你能想象吗？

sentences.en: We are giving people a tiny little intervention and it is producing a shift, but the shift does not laSt. Isn't that a wonderful thing?
sentences.zh: 我们给人们一个小小的干预，它确实产生了一个转变，但这个转变并不持久。这难道不是一件美妙的事情吗？

sentences.en: Because think about all the, apologize for the word, the crap that we hear all the time, you know?
sentences.zh: 因为想想所有那些，请原谅我用这个词，我们一直听到的废话，你知道吗？

sentences.en: Imagine if that were to stick forever.
sentences.zh: 想象一下如果那些东西永远挥之不去。

sentences.en: You wouldn't want that kind of a brain.
sentences.zh: 你不会想要那样的大脑。

sentences.en: So our brains change, our minds change, associations move around, but they always will gravitate to whatever is your cultural default.
sentences.zh: 所以我们的大脑会改变，我们的思想会改变，联想会四处移动，但它们总是会向你所在的文化默认值靠拢。

sentences.en: And so to bring about actual change, society around us has to change.
sentences.zh: 因此，要实现真正的改变，我们周围的社会必须改变。

sentences.en: And then we will move and then the default will be a new default.
sentences.zh: 然后我们就会随之改变，默认值就会变成一个新的默认值。

sentences.en: So I'm not bothered by this result.
sentences.zh: 所以我并不为这个结果感到困扰。

sentences.en: I would never predict that the effect should last very long because it would be a dangerous thing if the effects lasted long because
sentences.zh: 我从不预测这种效果会持续很长时间，因为如果效果持续太久会是一件危险的事情，因为

sentences.en: we don't get to choose everything we see and hear.
sentences.zh: 我们无法选择我们看到和听到的一切。

sentences.en: So it's a good thing that we get to snap back to something.
sentences.zh: 所以能弹回到某种状态是一件好事。

sentences.en: So you've been studying implicit bias for decades now, and you have found some evidence that in recent years, some of our biases have decreased.
sentences.zh: 所以你研究内隐偏见已经几十年了，你发现了一些证据表明，近年来，我们的一些偏见有所减少。

sentences.en: What is happening?
sentences.zh: 发生了什么？

sentences.en: How has that happened?
sentences.zh: 这是怎么发生的？

sentences.en: How are we measuring it?
sentences.zh: 我们是如何测量它的？

sentences.en: And what are the biases that are different than they might've been 10 or 20 years ago?
sentences.zh: 与 10 或 20 年前相比，现在的偏见有什么不同？

sentences.en: It is among the most exciting work that's been happening in my lab.
sentences.zh: 这是我实验室里发生的最令人兴奋的工作之一。

sentences.en: And the person to credit here is a brilliant postdoc, also was a graduate student, Tessa Charlesworth.
sentences.zh: 这里要归功的人是一位出色的博士后，她也曾是我的研究生，Tessa Charlesworth。

sentences.en: As you know, we opened the website where implicit bias tests were made available in 1998.
sentences.zh: 如你所知，我们在 1998 年开设了提供内隐偏见测试的网站。

sentences.en: And here's the story about the beginning of it.
sentences.zh: 这是关于它起源的故事。

sentences.en: There was very little on the internet.
sentences.zh: 当时互联网上几乎没什么东西。

sentences.en: There was no psychology experiment happening on the internet.
sentences.zh: 互联网上没有心理学实验。

sentences.en: The internet was not very well developed.
sentences.zh: 互联网当时还不是很发达。

sentences.en: People then, even large corporations would have kind of one picture with their name and some URL and some phone numbers.
sentences.zh: 那时人们，甚至大公司，通常只有一张照片，写着名字、网址和一些电话号码。

sentences.en: That was what was on the internet.
sentences.zh: 那就是互联网上的内容。

sentences.en: And, you know, here we are, we say, let's put these tests on the internet.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，我们当时说，把这些测试放到互联网上吧。

sentences.en: After four years of testing it internally in the lab, once we felt we had a good handle on
sentences.zh: 在实验室内部测试了四年之后，一旦我们觉得我们很好地掌握了

sentences.en: what it was doing and all the variations that we needed to do to establish basic issues, we put these
sentences.zh: 它在做什么，以及我们需要做的所有变体来确立基本问题，我们就把这些

sentences.en: tests on a website and we thought, and I remember very explicitly saying to my two colleagues, Tony
sentences.zh: 测试放到了网站上，我们想，我非常清楚地记得我对我的两位同事 Tony

sentences.en: Greenwald and Brian Nosek, who actually built the website, I said to them, wouldn't it be amazing?
sentences.zh: Greenwald 和 Brian Nosek 说，是他们真正建立了这个网站，我对他们说，这难道不神奇吗？

sentences.en: Like, we don't have to bring one subject in at a time.
sentences.zh: 就像，我们不必一次只带一个受试者进来。

sentences.en: And maybe in a year, we'll have 500 people who will have taken this test and will have so much data and they won't even be, you know, Yale and
sentences.zh: 也许一年内，我们会有 500 人参加这个测试，我们将拥有如此多的数据，而且他们甚至不会是，你知道，耶鲁大学和

sentences.en: University of Washington students.
sentences.zh: 华盛顿大学的学生。

sentences.en: So people will actually have to take these data seriously because they will come from real people, not from college students.
sentences.zh: 所以人们将不得不认真对待这些数据，因为它们来自真实的人，而不是大学生。

sentences.en: I mean, we were so naive because in the very first month after the site opened, we had 45,000 completed tests.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我们太天真了，因为在网站开通后的第一个月，我们就完成了 45,000 次测试。

sentences.en: And we, you know, we were not only taken aback, we, we had to figure out a coping strategy because people were now writing to us
sentences.zh: 而且我们，你知道，我们不仅感到吃惊，我们还必须想出一个应对策略，因为人们现在每天给我们写

sentences.en: dozens of messages in a given day.
sentences.zh: 几十条信息。

sentences.en: Your test is stupid.
sentences.zh: 你们的测试很愚蠢。

sentences.en: You know, I am not, I do not have a race bias.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我不是，我没有种族偏见。

sentences.en: I am a rap musician.
sentences.zh: 我是一名说唱音乐家。

sentences.en: How dare you tell me?
sentences.zh: 你怎么敢这么说我？

sentences.en: So, so this is what we had to deal with.
sentences.zh: 所以，所以这就是我们必须处理的事情。

sentences.en: Anyway, to make a long story short, you know, we think something like maybe we don't count anymore, but there are at least 40 million tests have been now taken.
sentences.zh: 总之，长话短说，你知道，我们认为有些东西可能我们不再计算了，但现在至少已经进行了 4000 万次测试。

sentences.en: And we have an awful lot of data from about 2007, because we were fiddling with things and we were just getting used to how to build it.
sentences.zh: 而且我们有大量从 2007 年左右开始的数据，因为我们当时在摆弄各种东西，刚开始习惯如何构建它。

sentences.en: We don't believe that the data we got before 2007 were as stable, as reliable, as good as the data from 2007 onwards.
sentences.zh: 我们不认为 2007 年之前得到的数据像 2007 年以后的数据那样稳定、可靠和优秀。

sentences.en: So from there onwards, there are lots of data and the group has put these data on a public website.
sentences.zh: 所以从那时起，有了大量的数据，团队已经把这些数据放到了一个公共网站上。

sentences.en: So anybody can go there, anybody can take those data and analyze them.
sentences.zh: 所以任何人都可以去那里，任何人都可以拿走这些数据并进行分析。

sentences.en: And in fact, many people have.
sentences.zh: 事实上，很多人已经这么做了。

sentences.en: So Tessa Charlesworth decided to look at what has happened over time.
sentences.zh: 所以 Tessa Charlesworth 决定看看随着时间的推移发生了什么。

sentences.en: These are not your typical psychological analyses, right?
sentences.zh: 这些不是你典型的心理学分析，对吧？

sentences.en: We do do some longitudinal work, developmental psychologists do study what happens to a child as the child develops and so on.
sentences.zh: 我们确实做了一些纵向研究，发展心理学家确实会研究孩子在成长过程中会发生什么等等。

sentences.en: But this data set, I think is so generous.
sentences.zh: 但我认为这个数据集太慷慨了。

sentences.en: There is no such database where we've been collecting data
sentences.zh: 没有这样的数据库，我们一直在收集数据

sentences.en: continuously 24 seven for since 2007 to today.
sentences.zh: 从 2007 年到现在，全天候 24/7 不间断地收集。

sentences.en: So it's just unusual, you know, a Gallup poll, however wonderful it might be, is going to go in and in a single moment, get data from 2,500 people
sentences.zh: 所以这很不寻常，你知道，盖洛普民意调查，无论它多么出色，它都会在某一时刻，从 2,500 人那里获取数据

sentences.en: or whatever, and then conclude that Americans do this or that.
sentences.zh: 或者类似的情况，然后得出美国人这样做或那样的结论。

sentences.en: We're collecting data every second, every minute, you know, of the day and night, because we also opened a bunch of international sites.
sentences.zh: 我们每秒、每分钟都在收集数据，你知道，日日夜夜，因为我们也开设了一堆国际站点。

sentences.en: And so truly data are being collected around, around the clock.
sentences.zh: 所以数据确实是在全天候收集的。

sentences.en: And we have for many tests, take race, which is a very popular teSt. We now have data from dozens and dozens of people in every little location, every county of the United States.
sentences.zh: 而且我们有很多测试，以种族为例，这是一个非常受欢迎的测试。我们现在拥有美国每个小地方、每个县成千上万人的数据。

sentences.en: So what we can say is, okay, we've got that big, big fat pool of data.
sentences.zh: 所以我们可以说，好的，我们有那个庞大的数据池。

sentences.en: Can we look to see if anything has changed in 2007 to today?
sentences.zh: 我们可以看看 2007 年到现在有什么变化吗？

sentences.en: And again, I should tell you, I was hesitant about even taking this on because I was so persuaded that implicit
sentences.zh: 再说一次，我应该告诉你，我甚至对承担这项任务感到犹豫，因为我太确信内隐

sentences.en: bias cannot change in the long term that I thought, okay, do it, do this as an exercise for
sentences.zh: 偏见在长期内无法改变，所以我心想，好吧，做吧，把这当作你统计学课程的一个练习，

sentences.en: your statistics class, but it's not really something that, you know, we'll be able to say anything about.
sentences.zh: 但这并不是真正我们能说出什么名堂的东西。

sentences.en: And we will be able to say, I think, nothing has changed.
sentences.zh: 而且我想，我们能说的就是，什么都没变。

sentences.en: It's implicit bias in my mind, having looked at the data, having studied it for about 20 years by then, more than that, 30 years, maybe.
sentences.zh: 在我看来，在看过这些数据，研究了大约 20 年之后，不止于此，也许 30 年，它是内隐偏见。

sentences.en: I was quite persuaded that we would see flat lines over time, 2007 to when we first did the analysis, 2016, no change.
sentences.zh: 我相当确信我们会看到随时间推移的平线，从 2007 年到我们第一次进行分析的 2016 年，没有变化。

sentences.en: And maybe we should write about that.
sentences.zh: 也许我们应该写写这个。

sentences.en: Maybe we should say, look, implicit bias is not changing, et cetera.
sentences.zh: 也许我们应该说，看，内隐偏见没有改变，等等。

sentences.en: So Tessa not only did the analysis, she did it not just for one or two groups, but for six of them.
sentences.zh: 所以 Tessa 不仅做了分析，她不仅为一两个群体做了分析，而是为六个群体做了分析。

sentences.en: She looked at anti-gay bias.
sentences.zh: 她研究了反同性恋偏见。

sentences.en: She looked at, you know, race bias.
sentences.zh: 她研究了，你知道，种族偏见。

sentences.en: She looked at skin tone bias, which is different than race bias, of course, age bias, disability, and body weight bias.
sentences.zh: 她研究了肤色偏见，这当然不同于种族偏见，还有年龄偏见、残疾偏见和体重偏见。

sentences.en: So there are six different kinds of categories.
sentences.zh: 所以有六种不同的类别。

sentences.en: And what she discovered that surprised us is that on three of those tests, you do see substantial change.
sentences.zh: 她发现令我们惊讶的是，在其中三个测试中，你确实看到了实质性的变化。

sentences.en: I'll begin with the one that showed such big change that we're still gobsmacked from having seen those data.
sentences.zh: 我先从那个显示出如此巨大变化的一个开始，我们看到那些数据时至今仍感到震惊。

sentences.en: And that's anti-gay bias.
sentences.zh: 那就是反同性恋偏见。

sentences.en: So anti-gay bias has dropped off by 64% between 2007 and 2020.
sentences.zh: 所以反同性恋偏见在 2007 年到 2020 年间下降了 64%。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: How can this be?
sentences.zh: 这怎么可能？

sentences.en: How can a bias that was so high in 2007, it was one of the large biases, okay?
sentences.zh: 一种在 2007 年如此之高的偏见怎么可能下降，它是当时的大偏见之一，好吗？

sentences.en: Gay, bad, straight, good.
sentences.zh: 同性恋，坏；异性恋，好。

sentences.en: How come that bias has been just withering away at this speed?
sentences.zh: 这种偏见为何能以如此快的速度逐渐消退？

sentences.en: And remarkably, if you look at any demographic group in the country, you can look at elderly people, young people, you
sentences.zh: 值得注意的是，如果你观察国内的任何人口群体，无论是老年人、年轻人，

sentences.en: can look at people who live on the coast in the middle of the country, the North, the South, the rich, the poor, the educated, the less educated.
sentences.zh: 还是住在沿海地区、中部地区、北方、南方的人，无论贫富，受教育程度高低，

sentences.en: You can look at any of these.
sentences.zh: 观察任何群体都是如此。

sentences.en: And we see change in every single group.
sentences.zh: 我们看到每一个群体都在发生变化。

sentences.en: So everybody's changing on this.
sentences.zh: 所以每个人都在这方面有所改变。

sentences.en: Yes, there are two groups that are changing faster than everybody.
sentences.zh: 是的，有两个群体的变化速度比其他所有人都快。

sentences.en: Your listeners should try to predict what those groups might be.
sentences.zh: 你的听众不妨猜猜是哪两个群体。

sentences.en: And as they do that,
sentences.zh: 在他们思考的同时，

sentences.en: I'll give the answer.
sentences.zh: 我来公布答案。

sentences.en: Younger people are changing faster.
sentences.zh: 年轻人变化得更快。

sentences.en: And people who are self-professed liberals, are also changing faster.
sentences.zh: 自认为是自由派的人，变化也更快。

sentences.en: In fact, those two groups have pulled away from their original bias in 2007 so fast that they are today at neutrality.
sentences.zh: 事实上，这两个群体自2007年以来摆脱原有偏见的速度非常快，以至于今天他们已经处于中立状态。

sentences.en: For them, gay and straight are equally good and bad.
sentences.zh: 对他们来说，同性恋和异性恋在好坏评价上已无区别。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: The rest of us will catch up.
sentences.zh: 我们其他人也会迎头赶上的。

sentences.en: So one of the nice things about this analysis, these are called time series analysis.
sentences.zh: 这种分析的一个优点在于，它被称为时间序列分析。

sentences.en: And we use a particular model called ARIMA for those who might want to go look up what it is.
sentences.zh: 我们使用了一种名为ARIMA的特定模型，感兴趣的人可以去查查这是什么。

sentences.en: There are lots of limitations to this method.
sentences.zh: 这种方法有很多局限性。

sentences.en: We have to make very sure that we're not just showing this effect because all of a sudden in recent years, there are many more young people taking the test than they were before.
sentences.zh: 我们必须非常确定，我们展示的这种效应并非仅仅是因为近年来参加测试的年轻人比以前多了很多。

sentences.en: That would not be a correct way to interpret the data to say there is change.
sentences.zh: 如果仅仅因为这个就说发生了变化，那不是解读数据的正确方式。

sentences.en: It's not really change.
sentences.zh: 那并不是真正的变化。

sentences.en: It's just that the sample has more young people today and didn't have as many young.
sentences.zh: 那只是因为今天的样本中年轻人更多，而以前没那么多。

sentences.en: So you have to rule out lots and lots of things.
sentences.zh: 所以你必须排除掉很多很多因素。

sentences.en: So if they're interested, they should go look at this paper that was published in psychological science and what they
sentences.zh: 如果他们感兴趣，应该去看看那篇发表在《心理科学》上的论文，当你深入研究数据时，

sentences.en: will see if you get into the data is that this change we think is real.
sentences.zh: 你会发现我们认为这种变化是真实的。

sentences.en: This is a real shift in what people are thinking.
sentences.zh: 这是人们思想上的真正转变。

sentences.en: And when I tell people that these days, they say, oh yes, of course, I could have predicted that that would happen.
sentences.zh: 如今当我告诉人们这一点时，他们会说，哦，是的，当然，我早就预料到会这样。

sentences.en: Well, you know, as we know, hindsight is 20-20 and they can.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你知道，正如我们所知，事后诸葛亮总是看得最清楚，他们确实能预料到。

sentences.en: But in in retrospect, I too now see why this might have happened.
sentences.zh: 但回过头来看，我现在也明白了为什么会发生这种情况。

sentences.en: So I would love for your listeners while we talk to be thinking about this.
sentences.zh: 所以我希望你的听众在我们交谈时也能思考这个问题。

sentences.en: Why did sexuality bias change?
sentences.zh: 为什么性取向偏见会发生变化？

sentences.en: Because no other bias has changed as faSt. Race bias has changed, but by 25%.
sentences.zh: 因为没有其他偏见变化得这么快。种族偏见确实有所改变，但只有25%。

sentences.en: Okay, so good news is it has moved.
sentences.zh: 好的，好消息是它确实有所动摇。

sentences.en: But we can ask, why not at the level of 64%?
sentences.zh: 但我们可以问，为什么不是64%的程度呢？

sentences.en: We know that's possible.
sentences.zh: 我们知道那是可能的。

sentences.en: So why is race slow?
sentences.zh: 那么为什么种族偏见改变得这么慢？

sentences.en: Why is skin tone bias going down again by 25%?
sentences.zh: 为什么肤色偏见又只下降了25%？

sentences.en: Why is it not as fast as sexuality?
sentences.zh: 为什么它不像性取向偏见那样快？

sentences.en: We know that gender bias, home and career bias has come down by about that much.
sentences.zh: 我们知道性别偏见，即家庭与职业偏见，也下降了大约那么多。

sentences.en: But why so slow?
sentences.zh: 但为什么这么慢？

sentences.en: The association that men are for STEM and science and math and women okay for arts and so on, that bias has also shifted, but not as much as the anti-gay bias has.
sentences.zh: 那种认为男性适合STEM、科学和数学，女性适合艺术之类的刻板印象，这种偏见也发生了转变，但没有反同性恋偏见转变的那么多。

sentences.en: There are three biases that have not shifted much at all, in fact.
sentences.zh: 事实上，有三种偏见几乎完全没有改变。

sentences.en: And that's anti-elderly bias, which continues on and is absolutely stable, a little bit lower, but not anything to write home about.
sentences.zh: 那就是反老年人偏见，它持续存在且绝对稳定，虽然稍微降低了一点，但没什么值得大书特书的。

sentences.en: Disability bias, just flat since 2007, no change.
sentences.zh: 残疾偏见，自2007年以来一直持平，没有变化。

sentences.en: And body weight bias, a bias against people who are overweight.
sentences.zh: 还有体重偏见，即对超重人群的偏见。

sentences.en: That remains flat.
sentences.zh: 这依然保持不变。

sentences.en: And that looks like the hardest one in some ways in the data that will change.
sentences.zh: 在数据中，这看起来在某些方面是最难改变的一种。

sentences.en: We think these biases are going to be around.
sentences.zh: 我们认为这些偏见还会存在下去。

sentences.en: If they move at this rate, we're not going to see change for 200 years.
sentences.zh: 如果按这个速度发展，我们200年内都不会看到什么变化。

sentences.en: That's our prediction.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们的预测。

sentences.en: So then what is it that's special about anti-gay bias?
sentences.zh: 那么反同性恋偏见有什么特别之处呢？

sentences.en: And I'd like to put a few ideas out and then see if your listeners would agree.
sentences.zh: 我想提出几个观点，看看你的听众是否同意。

sentences.en: I think that sexuality bias changed because it became personal in some way.
sentences.zh: 我认为性取向偏见之所以改变，是因为它在某种程度上变得个人化了。

sentences.en: That is to say, parents and grandparents, friends, neighbors, cousins, we all discovered that people who were close to us said to us, I'm gay.
sentences.zh: 也就是说，父母、祖父母、朋友、邻居、堂表亲，我们都发现身边亲近的人对我们说：我是同性恋。

sentences.en: That became possible.
sentences.zh: 这变得可能了。

sentences.en: And as they began to come out, we would have confronted a state of cognitive dissonance, this old idea in psychology.
sentences.zh: 当他们开始出柜时，我们就会面临心理学中那个古老的认知失调状态。

sentences.en: I believe being gay is bad.
sentences.zh: 我相信同性恋是不好的。

sentences.en: Here's my child saying she's gay.
sentences.zh: 现在我的孩子说她是同性恋。

sentences.en: I have to do something in my head to resolve this conflict.
sentences.zh: 我必须在脑子里做点什么来解决这个冲突。

sentences.en: And Leon Festinger, the genius in the 1950s who wrote about this theory of cognitive dissonance said, we can't maintain these.
sentences.zh: 20世纪50年代提出认知失调理论的天才莱昂·费斯廷格说过，我们无法维持这种状态。

sentences.en: We have to change one or the other.
sentences.zh: 我们必须改变其中之一。

sentences.en: Either you have to cut off relations with your child and say, I disown you, or you can begin to say, I think being gay is not the horrible
sentences.zh: 要么你必须断绝与孩子的关系，说我与你断绝关系，要么你开始说，我想同性恋也许不像圣经告诉我的那样可怕，

sentences.en: thing that the Bible told me or whatever, however you came to those beliefs.
sentences.zh: 或者无论你当初是如何形成那些信念的。

sentences.en: And what we have found is that maybe it would have gone the other way.
sentences.zh: 而我们发现，事情也可能走向另一个方向。

sentences.en: I had this happen two centuries ago, but given the time in which we live and the meaning of what religion is to many of us, where we believe that it might be
sentences.zh: 这种情况在两个世纪前也发生过，但考虑到我们所处的时代以及宗教对我们许多人的意义，我们认为它可能是

sentences.en: a guide to certain ways of living a good life, but that we may not want to take the Bible so literally or whatever.
sentences.zh: 过上美好生活的指南，但我们可能不想那么字面地去解读圣经，等等。

sentences.en: It just so happened that people went with love.
sentences.zh: 结果人们选择了爱。

sentences.en: The love of the child, the love of your neighbor or your friend trumped this other belief.
sentences.zh: 对孩子的爱，对邻居或朋友的爱，战胜了这种旧有的信念。

sentences.en: And so we've seen change.
sentences.zh: 所以我们看到了变化。

sentences.en: This does not happen for anti-elderly bias, for race, where we are so segregated.
sentences.zh: 这种情况并没有发生在反老年人偏见或种族偏见上，因为我们在这些方面太隔离了。

sentences.en: I mean, think about race.
sentences.zh: 我是说，想想种族问题。

sentences.en: You know, the two big domains in which we live and do our stuff are home, the neighborhood, the family, and work.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们生活和活动的两个主要领域是家庭、社区、亲属关系，以及工作。

sentences.en: And in both those domains, we're deeply segregated by race.
sentences.zh: 在这两个领域中，我们都存在严重的种族隔离。

sentences.en: We just don't see people across race lines because it gets intersected with socioeconomic class and so on.
sentences.zh: 我们就是看不到跨种族的人，因为这与社会经济阶层等因素交织在一起。

sentences.en: So the chance that you would meet that person and have the same kind of experience that, you know, straight parents and straight
sentences.zh: 所以，你遇到那样的人并拥有同样经历的机会，你知道，异性恋父母和异性恋

sentences.en: grandparents had to deal with when the time came, that just is not an opportunity that race offers us.
sentences.zh: 祖父母在那个时刻不得不面对的那种经历，种族问题并没有给我们提供这样的机会。

sentences.en: So as a society, we have to ask ourselves, what will we do if we care about race bias?
sentences.zh: 因此，作为一个社会，我们必须自问，如果我们关心种族偏见，我们该怎么办？

sentences.en: The second thing that happened for sexuality is that Hollywood got involved.
sentences.zh: 性取向偏见发生改变的第二个原因是好莱坞的介入。

sentences.en: Institutions are deeply important.
sentences.zh: 制度极其重要。

sentences.en: To Hollywood, this particular dimension matters because there's a larger number of gay people in the entertainment industry than many other industries.
sentences.zh: 对好莱坞来说，这个维度很重要，因为娱乐业中的同性恋人数比许多其他行业都要多。

sentences.en: I think they cared about it.
sentences.zh: 我认为他们很在乎这一点。

sentences.en: So they did something remarkable.
sentences.zh: 所以他们做了一件了不起的事情。

sentences.en: They made movies and they made TV shows, not just ordinary ones, but ones in which the gay character would be cooler and smarter and nicer than the straight people on the show.
sentences.zh: 他们制作了电影和电视节目，不仅是普通的节目，而且是那种同性恋角色比剧中异性恋角色更酷、更聪明、更友善的节目。

sentences.en: And I don't know, people watched those and came to see that this was being normalized.
sentences.zh: 我不知道，人们看了这些节目，开始意识到这正在变得常态化。

sentences.en: And we're very sensitive to that.
sentences.zh: 我们对此非常敏感。

sentences.en: What do other people in our culture think?
sentences.zh: 我们文化中的其他人怎么想？

sentences.en: If I hear that, you know, 90% of my neighbors are saving energy by doing certain things, I become very competitive and I want to be better than them and I will do it.
sentences.zh: 如果我听说，你知道，我90%的邻居都在通过做某些事情来节能，我会变得非常有竞争意识，我想比他们做得更好，我也会去做。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Much more so than if you ask me to be a good person and care about the environment.
sentences.zh: 这比你要求我做一个好人并关心环境要有效得多。

sentences.en: That doesn't do very much.
sentences.zh: 那样做效果不大。

sentences.en: But hearing that other people do.
sentences.zh: 但听说别人也在做。

sentences.en: We're very competitive.
sentences.zh: 我们非常有竞争意识。

sentences.en: They're very competitive, especially socially, of course.
sentences.zh: 他们非常有竞争意识，当然，特别是在社交方面。

sentences.en: So I think that that helped a great deal.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为这起到了很大的帮助。

sentences.en: And then, of course, the hand of government came in.
sentences.zh: 当然，政府之手也介入了。

sentences.en: The Massachusetts Supreme Court first said gay marriages legalized.
sentences.zh: 马萨诸塞州最高法院首先宣布同性婚姻合法化。

sentences.en: I remember I had moved to Cambridge only a couple of years before this happened.
sentences.zh: 我记得在这件事发生前几年，我才搬到剑桥。

sentences.en: And Boston announced that it would open its courtrooms on whatever it was,
sentences.zh: 波士顿宣布它将在某个时间开放法庭，

sentences.en: Monday morning at 9 a.m.
sentences.zh: 周一早上9点，

sentences.en: and perform the first gay marriages.
sentences.zh: 并举行首批同性婚礼。

sentences.en: And Cambridge, the suburb, not wanting to be second, decided that it would open its courtrooms at one minute past midnight to be the first city to do it.
sentences.zh: 而剑桥这个郊区城市，不想落后，决定在午夜过一分钟就开放法庭，成为第一个这样做的城市。

sentences.en: So having lived in a town that was the first and having stood there watching the first gay married couples walking out.
sentences.zh: 所以，生活在一个率先这样做的城镇，并站在那里看着第一对同性伴侣走出来。

sentences.en: It was clear that this was a moment.
sentences.zh: 很明显，这是一个重要的时刻。

sentences.en: Something historic had just happened.
sentences.zh: 历史性的一刻刚刚发生。

sentences.en: So now think about this.
sentences.zh: 现在思考一下。

sentences.en: How many times in our history has change come about at three different levels?
sentences.zh: 在我们的历史上，有多少次变革是在三个不同层面上同时发生的？

sentences.en: The individual, the organizational or institutional, and at the level of governmental policies and the law within a short period of time.
sentences.zh: 个人层面、组织或机构层面，以及政府政策和法律层面，在短时间内同时发生。

sentences.en: You know, yes, the civil rights movement in the 60s did something at that third level.
sentences.zh: 你知道，是的，60年代的民权运动在第三个层面上做了一些事情。

sentences.en: But I don't think that we changed much at the institutional or individual levels.
sentences.zh: 但我认为我们在机构或个人层面上并没有发生太大变化。

sentences.en: So it could not have the same impact as I think this did.
sentences.zh: 所以它不可能产生我认为这次变革所产生的那种影响。

sentences.en: So this is a very important lesson for us, that if we want to make change, maybe one of the messages from our research is that try and do it at all three levels.
sentences.zh: 所以这对我们来说是一个非常重要的教训，如果我们想做出改变，也许我们研究传达的信息之一就是尝试在所有三个层面上进行。

sentences.en: And for that reason, I think we should be pleased that people in our society today use the word systemic so much more than we have.
sentences.zh: 正因如此，我认为我们应该感到高兴，因为当今社会的人们使用“系统性”这个词的频率比以前高多了。

sentences.en: Systemic does not mean systematic.
sentences.zh: 系统性（systemic）并不意味着系统化（systematic）。

sentences.en: Systemic means that the system needs to get engaged.
sentences.zh: 系统性意味着系统需要参与进来。

sentences.en: And I would like to argue that the system consists of individual people.
sentences.zh: 我想说的是，系统是由个人组成的。

sentences.en: The system consists of institutions.
sentences.zh: 系统是由机构组成的。

sentences.en: The system consists of large governmental organizations that can move certain kinds of levers.
sentences.zh: 系统是由能够推动某些杠杆的大型政府组织组成的。

sentences.en: I cannot say that one is more important than the other, but I would like to argue that if we go for system change, we will see change a lot faster.
sentences.zh: 我不能说哪一个比另一个更重要，但我认为如果我们追求系统性变革，我们将看到变化发生得快得多。

sentences.en: Well, Dr. Banaji, this has been amazingly interesting.
sentences.zh: 嗯，Banaji博士，这真是太有趣了。

sentences.en: I really appreciate your taking the time and explaining all of this to our listeners.
sentences.zh: 我非常感谢您抽出时间向我们的听众解释这一切。

sentences.en: I'm sure that they're going to enjoy hearing all of this and taking the IAT.
sentences.zh: 我相信他们会喜欢听这一切，并参加IAT测试。

sentences.en: We'll get you some more data, I promise.
sentences.zh: 我保证会为您提供更多数据。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And I'll get lots of little nasty notes at the end of that.
sentences.zh: 而且最后我会收到很多刻薄的小纸条。

sentences.en: Oh, I hope not.
sentences.zh: 哦，我希望不会。

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 不会的。

sentences.en: Actually, I should mention that the site is incredibly successful.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我应该提到这个网站非常成功。

sentences.en: I mean, the very moving letters that we have received, even from people who initially did not approve of the result that they got.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我们收到了非常感人的信件，甚至来自那些最初不认可自己测试结果的人。

sentences.en: And that is what gives me such faith in human beings, that the same people who wrote to us
sentences.zh: 这正是让我对人类充满信心的原因，那些写信给我们

sentences.en: to say pretty nasty things will write back later and say, I just had this experience and I wanted you to know that I understood what your stupid test was trying to tell me.
sentences.zh: 说些刻薄话的人，后来又写信回来说，我刚刚有了这种经历，我想让你知道，我理解了你们那个愚蠢的测试试图告诉我什么。

sentences.en: Success.
sentences.zh: 成功。

sentences.en: Thanks very much for having me.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢您邀请我。

sentences.en: It's a pleasure.
sentences.zh: 这是我的荣幸。
